articles.title: The 10 safest states in the US — and the 10 least safe
articles.summary: A report released by the personal finance website WalletHub evaluated all 50 US states, ranking them from the most to least safe.
articles.body:
WalletHub released a report ranking the safest states in the US.

States were ranked based on 52 safety indicators, including work safety and emergency preparedness.

Vermont and Massachusetts scored the highest. Mississippi and Louisiana scored the lowest.

Safe to say , safety comes in many forms beyond crime.

The ability to prepare well for an emergency situation is a form of security, as is the number of emergency responders available nearby. One's financial well-being amid fear of job loss and inflation is also relative to one's sense of safety.

A report released by the personal finance website WalletHub on Monday evaluated all 50 US states, ranking them from the most to least safe.

For each state, WalletHub examined 52 indicators across five categories: personal and residential safety, financial safety, road safety, workplace safety, and emergency preparedness.

The personal and residential safety category included factors such as crime rates, emergency responders per capita, and neighborhood watch groups per capita.

To evaluate financial safety , WalletHub looked at factors such as unemployment rates, median credit scores, identity-theft complaints per capita, and poverty rates.

The road safety ranking was determined by each state's rates of traffic fatalities and DUIs, road quality, and share of uninsured drivers, among other factors.

WalletHub's workplace safety ranking included examining the number of fatal occupational injuries per 100,000 full-time workers and the presence of Occupational Safety and Health Act plans.

Finally, the emergency preparedness ranking looked at states' histories of climate disasters.

WalletHub used data from sources such as the US Census Bureau, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Department of Labor, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the Crime Victims Center, among others.

Here are the 10 safest states in the US, and the 10 least safe states.

WalletHub ranked Vermont as the safest state in the US.

Vermont's unemployment rate is 2.7% — one of the lowest in the country — which helped it place fourth in the financial safety ranking. It's also the state with the second-fewest reported identity theft complaints per capita.

The state's road safety ranking was the third-highest in the US, with the second-best road quality and the fifth-fewest traffic fatalities of any state.

Its workplace safety ranking also made the top 10, placing sixth overall.

Vermont placed 16th in the personal and residential safety ranking and 11th in emergency preparedness.

As the second-safest state in the US, Massachusetts ranked in the top 10 of nearly every category of WalletHub's analysis.

The state placed second in the personal and residential safety ranking, with low crime rates, including the eighth-fewest thefts and fourth-fewest murders of any state, according to the WalletHub report. Massachusetts also placed second in WalletHub's road safety ranking, eighth in financial safety, and ninth in emergency preparedness.

Its workplace safety ranking was the lowest, coming in at 23rd overall.

Maine's low crime rate propelled it into the top three safest states in the US. With the fewest mass shootings between 2024 and September 2026, the third-fewest murders per capita, and the fewest aggravated assaults per capita, it ranked fourth in personal and residential safety.

Maine ranked 16th in financial safety with an unemployment rate of 3.4% and the 12th-lowest poverty rate in the US.

It ranked 8th in road safety, 21st in workplace safety, and second in emergency preparedness.

New Hampshire was ranked the fourth-safest state in the US, but it had the highest financial safety ranking of any state.

It placed third in personal and residential safety and fourth in emergency preparedness.

New Hampshire's road safety and workplace safety rankings were lower, at 12th and 41st, respectively.

Connecticut's personal and residential safety ranking was the highest of any state.

It placed 21st in both the financial safety and the road safety rankings, 25th in workplace safety, and 15th in emergency preparedness.

Utah was ranked No. 1 in road safety, No. 3 in emergency preparedness, and No. 4 in workplace safety.

It placed 26th in financial safety and 35th in personal and residential safety.

Minnesota's workplace safety ranked second, road safety ranked sixth, and financial safety ranked seventh. The state's personal and residential safety and emergency preparedness both ranked 23rd.

WalletHub ranked Indiana 7th in personal and residential safety, 25th in financial safety, 11th in road safety, 10th in workplace safety, and 28th in emergency preparedness.

In Rhode Island, the state's personal and residential safety and emergency preparedness were both ranked eighth-best in the US. It placed 20th in financial safety, 16th in road safety, and 39th in workplace safety.

Hawaii rounded out WalletHub's list of the top 10 safest states in the US, placing 10th.

Hawaii performed well in financial safety, with the second-highest ranking of any state. Personal and residential safety ranked 20th, road safety 26th, workplace safety 22nd, and emergency preparedness 13th.

Keep reading for the bottom 10 states, which were ranked the least safe in the US.

Georgia ranked 34th and 35th in personal and residential safety and road safety, respectively.

It placed 47th in financial safety and has the second-highest share of uninsured people.

Alabama ranked 36th in personal and residential safety, 34th in financial safety, and 31st in road safety. It ranked 40th in emergency preparedness.

The state tied in the lowest unemployment rate with Vermont, North Dakota, Hawaii, and South Dakota.

In Colorado, personal and residential safety ranked 46th among US states.

The state placed 19th in financial safety, 41st in road safety, and 38th in workplace safety.

When reached by Business Insider, Colorado Gov. Jared Polis' press secretary Eric Maruyama questioned the methodology of WalletHub's ranking, saying in an email, "It's unclear why this ranking of safest to least safe states takes into account things like credit scores, college savings, and household emergency funds, which are very different things than public safety and crime."

Maruyama added that Colorado is "seeing major year-over-year reductions in crime in key areas" since Polis has "signed laws to fund law enforcement, invest in proactive crime prevention strategies, and toughen penalties for auto theft."

"From 2024 to 2025 violent crime dropped by 10.7%, aggravated assaults dropped by 9%, property crime decreased by 17.3%, and motor vehicle thefts plummeted by 36.8%," he said. "Our work is showing results and this is the kind of data Gov. Polis looks at when assessing how to make our state safer."

It ranked 23rd for financial safety and 29th for personal and residential safety.

In the emergency preparedness category, it ranked 41st.

In WalletHub's study, Oklahoma ranked 32nd for personal and residential safety and 41st for financial safety.

It has the third-highest share of uninsured people and ranked 44th in workplace safety, per the report.

Arkansas ranked 44th for personal and residential safety, and 43rd in financial safety.

It has the fourth-most fatalities per 100 million vehicle miles of travel, and is ranked 47th for assaults per capita, WalletHub reported.

Florida is ranked 31st for personal and residential safety.

The Sunshine State ranked 45th in financial safety, 46th in workplace safety, and 47th in emergency preparedness.

Texas is ranked 40th in personal and residential safety, financial safety, and road safety.

It ranked 48th in emergency preparedness in WalletHub's report and has the highest share of uninsured people.

Louisiana ranked 49th in financial safety and emergency preparedness. It's ranked 43rd for workplace safety.

WalletHub's rankings also show that Louisiana is tied with New Jersey and Wyoming for the most law-enforcement employees per capita, and the state has the third-most assaults per capita.

Ranked the least safe state in the US by WalletHub, Mississippi also ranked the lowest in financial, road, work, and emergency preparedness safety.

For personal and residential safety, however, it ranked in the middle: The state is the 22nd safest.

Mississippi has the highest fatalities per 100 million vehicle miles traveled, and it's tied with New Mexico for the second-lowest share of people with rainy-day funds.

Per WalletHub, the state tied with Florida, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Louisiana for the highest total loss amount from climate disasters per capita.

articles.title: Jaguar apresenta elétrico Type 01 em meio a polêmica de design. | G1
articles.standfirst: Modelo de luxo tem mais de 1.000 cv e custa US$ 130 mil nos Estados Unidos. Grupo JLR tenta dar novo rumo à marca inglesa enquanto reestrutura fábricas e futuros modelos.
articles.summary: Modelo de luxo tem mais de 1.000 cv e custa US$ 130 mil nos Estados Unidos. Grupo JLR tenta dar novo rumo à marca enquanto reestrutura fábricas e futuros modelos.
articles.body:
Jaguar apresenta o elétrico de luxo Type 01 em Nova York. — Foto: REUTERS/Mike Segar

A Jaguar apresentou nesta quarta-feira (7) em Nova York o Type 01, seu novo carro elétrico de quatro portas, com preço inicial de US$ 130.500 (R$ 648 mil em conversão direta). O modelo tem capô muito longo, não possui vidro traseiro e concentra uma série de recursos tecnológicos.

O lançamento marca, segundo a Jaguar, o início de uma nova geração de veículos da marca e de uma nova fase para a fabricante britânica, controlada pela indiana Tata Motors.

O preço elevado representa uma aposta no mercado norte-americano, onde a aceitação de carros elétricos tem sido menor do que na Europa.

Segundo a Reuters, a JLR, grupo ao qual a marca pertence, pretende aumentar o foco nos consumidores dos Estados Unidos enquanto enfrenta dificuldades no mercado europeu.

Entre os desafios estão a concorrência de carros chineses com preços mais baixos, custos relacionados a tarifas e interrupções provocadas pela guerra entre Estados Unidos e Israel contra o Irã.

O desenho do Type 01 busca inspiração nos esportivos Jaguar E-Type dos anos 1960, modelos que se tornaram valorizados entre colecionadores.

O modelo tem uma arquitetura elétrica de 850 volts, o que possibilita despejar mais de 1.000 cv de potência e uma recarga ultrarrápida de 350 kW.

Segundo a Jaguar, com este recurso de recarga é possível recuperar em apenas 13 minutos mais de 320 km de autonomia. A marca declara que o alcance total do Type 01 com as baterias de 118 kW cheias é de mais de 600 km.

A apresentação ocorre depois que a Jaguar mostrou, em 2024, o conceito Type 00 , usado como símbolo da reformulação da marca. O protótipo tinha pintura em tom de rosa forte e provocou críticas de entusiastas de carros e de alguns políticos.

Como parte de um plano de recuperação, a empresa anunciou no mês passado que pretende reduzir quase 10% de sua força de trabalho nos próximos dois anos, por meio de desligamentos voluntários.

A companhia também decidiu transformar toda a sua linha em veículos elétricos . A estratégia ocorre apesar de executivos do setor terem demonstrado dúvidas sobre o interesse de consumidores de maior poder aquisitivo por carros elétricos.

A transformação da Jaguar começou em novembro de 2024 , quando a marca abandonou o tradicional logotipo com o felino que acompanhava seus carros desde os anos 1950.

A nova identidade passou a priorizar o nome Jaguar, escrito em letras minúsculas, com tipografia mais arredondada e espaçamento maior entre as letras.

A empresa afirmou que a mudança fazia parte de um plano para tornar a marca relevante para uma nova geração.

A reformulação também estava ligada ao plano de transformar a Jaguar em uma marca totalmente elétrica.

Nova marca da Jaguar — Foto: divulgação/Jaguar

A reação nas redes sociais, porém, foi negativa. Muitos usuários questionaram a mudança e disseram preferir o retorno aos carros a combustão com motores V8.

Outros criticaram a tentativa de combinar carros elétricos voltados a um público mais jovem com referências à Pop Art dos anos 1950.

O carro chamou atenção pelo desenho. Enquanto algumas curvas remetem aos esportivos da Jaguar, a lateral apresenta linhas retas que lembram a picape Tesla Cybertruck.

Nas redes sociais, a apresentação não conseguiu reverter as críticas à nova fase da marca. Usuários compararam o protótipo a um climatizador e a uma geladeira. Também houve comentários apontando semelhanças com modelos de outras marcas, como Rolls-Royce, BMW e Porsche.

Conceito Jaguar Type 00 foi apresentado para ilustrar o futuro da marca. — Foto: divulgação/Jaguar

Em setembro de 2026, a Jaguar Land Rover anunciou outro movimento de grande impacto. A fabricante informou que eliminará cerca de 4 mil postos de trabalho , quase 10% de seu quadro, por meio de um programa de demissão voluntária ao longo dos dois anos seguintes.

A empresa pretende economizar 1,7 bilhão de libras, cerca de R$ 12,5 bilhões, e reduzir seu ponto de equilíbrio para aproximadamente 300 mil veículos.

A JLR emprega cerca de 43 mil pessoas em todo o mundo, sendo 34 mil no Reino Unido. A empresa não informou onde os cortes serão realizados.

A medida ocorre em meio à concorrência de fabricantes chineses e aos efeitos das tarifas comerciais. A fabricante também ainda se recuperava de um ataque cibernético ocorrido em 2025, que provocou uma longa paralisação da produção e afetou sua cadeia de fornecedores.

A reportagem do g1 conversou com o CEO da JLR no Brasil, João Oliveira, sobre a situação da fábrica do grupo em Porto Real (RJ).

A planta pode produzir os modelos Evoque e Discovery e tem capacidade de montar mais de 40 mil unidades por ano usando os três turnos.

Desde julho a linha de produção está parada. O Discovery foi descontinuado globalmente e a produção do Evoque até o fim de 2026 já foi feita. Ainda será definido o futuro do modelo no Brasil.

Os colaboradores da fábrica passam desde então por treinamentos de reciclagem. Não houve demissões no Brasil até o momento.

Mesmo com o corte de empregos, a JLR afirmou que pretende lançar cinco novos produtos nos 12 meses seguintes e manter investimentos entre 15 bilhões e 18 bilhões de libras, cerca de R$ 110,5 bilhões a R$ 132,6 bilhões, nos cinco anos seguintes.

Os recursos serão destinados à eletrificação, tecnologias digitais, manufatura avançada e melhorias na experiência do cliente.

O programa de demissão voluntária deverá atingir principalmente os 26 mil funcionários das áreas administrativa e de gestão. A empresa afirmou que precisa reduzir custos e simplificar sua estrutura para tornar o negócio mais resiliente.

articles.title: Influenciador troca festa de aniversário por plantio de 27 árvores | G1
articles.standfirst: Luiz Martins reuniu 15 amigos para plantar mudas de diferentes espécies em dois pontos da capital.
articles.summary: Luiz Martins reuniu 15 amigos para plantar mudas de diferentes espécies em dois pontos da capital.
articles.body:
O influenciador Luiz Martins decidiu trocar a tradicional festa de aniversário por uma ação ambiental. Para comemorar os 27 anos, ele plantou 27 árvores em diferentes pontos de Palmas nesta terça-feira (6). As mudas de seis espécies foram plantadas no Parque Cesamar e na Avenida LO-11, em frente à Feira do Bosque.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Luiz reuniu 15 amigos para realizar o plantio. "O meu objetivo principal era incentivar e continuar incentivando as pessoas a fazerem o mesmo no aniversário.”

Segundo o influenciador, a ideia também surgiu da relação que tem com a natureza e com o Tocantins. "Como tocantinense, eu sou apaixonado na fauna e na flora tocantinense." Foram plantadas mudas de oiti, jacarandá, guapeva, ingá, ipê e jucá.

Luiz espera que a iniciativa possa inspirar outras pessoas. O plantio foi feito seguindo orientações sobre os locais e as espécies escolhidas.

"Nós não podemos plantar um ipê ao lado de outro ipê. Por ser uma árvore grande e por ser uma árvore de copa larga, ela pode atrapalhar a outra que estiver ao lado."

Segundo ele, o grupo tomou os cuidados necessários para escolher os locais das mudas e permitir que elas tenham condições de crescer. Luiz também explicou que, em áreas urbanas, é importante verificar previamente as regras e buscar autorização dos órgãos responsáveis antes de realizar o plantio.

As 27 árvores foram distribuídas entre o Parque Cesamar e a Avenida LO-11, em frente à Feira do Bosque.

A Fundação Municipal de Meio Ambiente (FMA) de Palmas informou que considera admirável a iniciativa do influenciador, que procurou o órgão para solicitar autorização para o plantio das árvores e também recebeu orientações técnicas sobre a forma adequada para realizar a ação.

"A FMA esclarece que o plantio de árvores em áreas públicas deve ser previamente autorizado pelo órgão responsável, justamente para que sejam observados aspectos como a escolha das espécies, o local adequado e a forma correta de plantio, garantindo o desenvolvimento das mudas e evitando possíveis conflitos com calçadas, redes de infraestrutura e demais equipamentos urbanos", diz a nota.

Foram plantadas espécies como ipê, oiti, jacarandá, guapeva, ingá e jucá — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Luiz Martins

articles.title: Carnavalesco Milton Cunha é confirmado no festival Love Noronha | G1
articles.standfirst: Festival LGBTQIA será realizado de 28 de outubro a 2 de novembro e terá festa de Halloween inspirada nas lendas de Fernando de Noronha.
articles.summary: Festival LGBTQIA será realizado de 28 de outubro a 2 de novembro e terá festa de Halloween inspirada nas lendas de Fernando de Noronha.
articles.body:
O carnavalesco Milton Cunha, jurado do quadro Dança dos Famosos , do programa Domingão , da TV Globo , confirmou participação no festival LGBTQIA+ Love Noronha . O evento será realizado em Fernando de Noronha entre os dias 28 de outubro e 2 de novembro ( veja vídeo acima) .

Milton Cunha vai desembarcar na ilha acompanhado do companheiro, Vitor Moraes. Será a primeira visita do carnavalesco à ilha. “Fernando de Noronha, que alegria! O sonho de toda uma vida conhecer a ilha e agora vou para o festival Love Noronha, famosérrimo, alegríssimo e glamoroso”, disse Milton.

Cunha agradeceu o convite para o evento e afirmou que conhecer Fernando de Noronha era um projeto de vida.

Milton Cunha visita Fernando de Noronha pela primeira vez — Foto: Rogério Fidalgo/AgNews

Pela primeira vez, o Love Noronha terá uma festa de Halloween, também conhecida como Dia das Bruxas. O evento será realizado na noite de 31 de outubro e terá como destaque as lendas de Fernando de Noronha.

A produtora do festival, Maria do Céu, contou que a programação foi inspirada em pesquisas da historiadora Marieta Borges, que morreu em 2019 . Marieta pesquisou as lendas de Noronha e publicou um livro sobre o tema.

Love Noronha movimenta a ilha — Foto: Love Noronha/Divulgação

Uma das lendas mais conhecidas de Fernando de Noronha é a da Alamoa, segundo as pesquisas de Marieta Borges. A personagem é descrita como uma mulher loira que seduzia homens em noites de lua cheia e depois os matava.

A Alamoa foi interpretada pela apresentadora Angélica em 1995, quando as lendas de Fernando de Noronha foram tema do desfile da escola de samba Estação Primeira de Mangueira, no Rio de Janeiro .

Para os organizadores, a participação de Milton Cunha no festival também ajuda a divulgar nacionalmente a cultura, as lendas de Noronha como destino turístico.

A primeira edição do Love Noronha foi realizada em agosto de 2012 e homenageou o aniversário da cantora Madonna, considerada um ícone da comunidade LGBTQIA+.

Ao longo dos anos, o Love Noronha também foi realizado em agosto. Desde 2025, o festival passou a acontecer em outubro.

Os ingressos para o evento estão disponíveis na plataforma Sympla e pelo Whatzapp (81) 997591612.

articles.title: Mãe e adolescente atingidas por árvore em ventania lembram desespero | G1
articles.standfirst: Lorena Nora da Silva, de 32 anos, e Ketellyn Vitória Nora da Silva, de 16, estavam em frente de casa, em São José do Rio Preto (SP), quando ouviram o barulho na árvore, mas não conseguiram correr a tempo.
articles.summary: Lorena e Ketellyn foram atingidas durante ventania em São José do Rio Preto. Após exames descartarem fraturas, elas relembram o desespero e o livramento.
articles.body:
Adolescente de 16 anos ficou imobilizada após queda de árvore em Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Lorena Nora da Silva/Arquivo pessoal

A mulher de 32 anos e a filha, de 16, que foram atingidas pela árvore que caiu durante uma ventania no bairro Duas Vendas, em São José do Rio Preto , no interior de SP, relembraram os momentos de desespero para tentar escapar do impacto.

Lorena Nora da Silva e Ketellyn Vitória Nora da Silva estavam do lado de fora da casa quando ouviram um forte barulho. Ao g1 , elas contaram que tentaram correr, mas não tiveram tempo para fugir.

Ketellyn Vitória Nora da Silva ficou com o pescoço imobilizado após ser atingida por árvore em Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Lorena Nora da Silva/Arquivo pessoal

“Foi um desespero, medo. O pior podia ter acontecido comigo e com minha filha. Na hora eu pedi para Deus pôr a mão na gente, que nada de tão grave ia acontecer”, lembra Lorena.

Os vizinhos ouviram os gritos de socorro e ajudaram no resgate das vítimas. Elas foram encaminhadas para a Santa Casa de Rio Preto. No domingo, a Defesa Civil enviou alertas nos celulares da população sobre as fortes rajadas de vento e temporal com possibilidade de granizo nas regiões de Rio Preto e Araçatuba.

O tronco atingiu principalmente a adolescente, que levou uma pancada na cabeça e na região da coluna e caiu de barriga no chão. Por causa do impacto, os médicos chegaram a suspeitar de uma fratura na coluna , segundo a mãe.

Ketellyn precisou ficar imobilizada e com o pescoço sem se movimentar enquanto aguardava o resultado da ressonância magnética. O exame, no entanto, descartou a fratura.

“Quando se fala em coluna, a gente já imagina tanta coisa. Meu Deus, foi um grande livramento. Nascemos de novo”, afirma a mãe.

Lorena também ficou ferida. Ela relatou que caiu sentada sobre uma das pernas e machucou o pé. A mãe e a adolescente receberam alta médica na segunda-feira (5) e agora se recuperam em casa.

Apesar de terem escapado de ferimentos mais graves, Lorena diz que o medo continua. Segundo ela, há outras árvores próximas à residência que estariam em condições ruins.

articles.title: Papa menciona Nossa Senhora Aparecida em audiência geral no Vaticano | G1
articles.standfirst: Leão XIV fez homenagem à padroeira do Brasil durante Audiência Geral do Vaticano, nesta quarta-feira (7). Pontífice não mencionou polêmicas envolvendo Nossa Senhora Aparecida durante a campanha para o 1º turno.
articles.summary: O papa Leão XIV fez uma homenagem à Nossa Senhora Aparecida durante a Audiência Geral no Vaticano nesta quarta-feira (7).
articles.body:
O papa Leão XIV passa no meio de fiéis na chegada para audiência geral na praça São Pedro, no Vaticano, em 7 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Remo Casilli/ Reuters

O papa Leão XIV fez uma homenagem à Nossa Senhora Aparecida durante a Audiência Geral no Vaticano nesta quarta-feira (7). Em discurso na Praça Sao Pedro, ele mencionou a padroeira do Brasil — que protagonizou polêmicas durante a campanha para o 1º turno das eleições, incluindo a divulgação de notícias falsas e uma batalha de decisões no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

O pontífice não mencionou a polêmica e fez referência ao dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, celebrado em 12 de outubro no Brasil.

“Uma saudação cordial aos peregrinos de língua portuguesa, em especial aos grupos vindos do Brasil e de Portugal. Queridos irmãos e irmãs, na próxima segunda-feira, 12 de outubro, celebra-se Nossa Senhora Aparecida, Padroeira do Brasil. Confio todos vocês e as suas famílias à sua intercessão maternal. Que Nossa Senhora os proteja sempre! Deus os abençoe!”

A polêmica envolvendo a padroeira do Brasil começou após publicações nas redes sociais atruibuindo a Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e a políticos de direita a intenção de retirar de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de Padroeira do Brasil.

👉 Atualmente, não há no Congresso nenhum projeto de lei para tirar a condição de padroeira do Brasil de Nossa Senhora Aparecida - o último, de 2007, foi arquivado. Também não existe movimento organizado de evangélicos com essa intenção.

A controvérsia chegou ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) e ao STF e provocou ainda um embate entre Flávio Bolsonaro e a Conferência Nacional dos Bispos do Brasil (CNBB). O candidato do PL afirmou que o PT criou uma "fake news" sobre Nossa Senhora Aparecida "com ajuda de gente de dentro" da CNBB. Ele não apresentou provas da participação de integrantes da entidade.

A CNBB rebateu a acusação e afirmou que não produziu, autorizou ou participou da elaboração ou divulgação de informações falsas relacionadas às eleições.

"Atribuir à CNBB participação em estruturas de produção ou disseminação de desinformação, sem fatos e provas que sustentem tal afirmação, atinge injustamente a instituição e não contribui para a serenidade e a responsabilidade que devem caracterizar o processo eleitoral. A mentira não se combate com outra mentira", afirmou a entidade na ocasião.

O Vaticano não se posicionou sobre o caso.

articles.title: Família de Dandara Couto, desaparecida em SP, diz que modelo saiu de casa para fazer tranças no cabelo e nunca mais voltou | G1
articles.standfirst: Ela foi vista pela última vez na região da Rua Cristiano Viana, em Pinheiros, na Zona Oeste da capital paulista.
articles.summary: Ela foi vista pela última vez na região da Rua Cristiano Viana, em Pinheiros, na Zona Oeste da capital paulista.
articles.body:
Amigos acreditam que Dandara Couto estava com o cabelo sem tranças quando desapareceu — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A modelo Dandara Couto, de 27 anos, está desaparecida desde a última segunda-feira (5) em São Paulo . Segundo familiares e amigos, ela foi vista pela última vez nas proximidades da Rua Cristiano Viana, em Pinheiros, na Zona Oeste da capital.

Thiago Miguel, amigo de Dandara, afirmou que ela pode estar sem as tranças que aparecem nas fotos publicadas nas redes sociais. “Ela provavelmente está com esse cabelo. Nas imagens do Instagram ela está de trança em todos, mas ela saiu de casa sem [tranças]”, disse.

De acordo com a família, Dandara mora no bairro e saiu de casa na segunda-feira para comprar pão. Ela voltou para a residência e, depois, saiu novamente para fazer tranças no cabelo. Desde então, não retornou.

“Ela sumiu na segunda-feira, saiu para comprar pão, voltou, depois saiu para fazer o cabelo, fazer trança no cabelo, e aí pronto, não voltou mais. Então, os amigos que moram com ela nos avisaram e estamos procurando ela para todos os lados”, contou a tia de Dandara, Lellete Couto, ao g1 .

Segundo a tia, Dandara mora em São Paulo há alguns anos por causa do trabalho. Ela atua para marcas no Brasil e também já trabalhou fora do país.

Uma publicação compartilhada por familiares e amigos informa que o último local conhecido de Dandara. Eles pedem que qualquer pessoa que tenha visto Dandara ou tenha informações sobre o paradeiro dela entre em contato.

articles.standfirst: Campopiano se considera "a maior inimiga das feministas de SP" e tornou-se conhecida por afirmar que "feminicídio não existe". No RS, Cherini foi eleita com bandeira de defesa a vítimas de violência doméstica.
articles.summary: Campopiano se considera "a maior inimiga das feministas de SP" e tornou-se conhecida por afirmar que "feminicídio não existe". No RS, Cherini foi eleita com bandeira de defesa a vítimas de violência doméstica.
articles.body:
A deputada estadual mais votada do Rio Grande do Sul , Adri Cherini ( PL ), criticou nesta terça-feira (6) sua colega de partido Eduarda Campopiano (PL) por declarações sobre feminicídio e violência contra a mulher. Campopiano foi a deputada estadual mais votada de São Paulo , com mais de 1,9 milhão de votos.

Cherini tem como principal bandeira a defesa às mulheres vítimas de violência doméstica . Já Campopiano se considera "a maior inimiga das feministas de São Paulo" e tornou-se conhecida por afirmar que "feminicídio não existe" e que a tipificação penal seria uma "armadilha semântica".

"Uma bobagem. Eu acho que ela precisa andar mais pelo estado dela e conhecer a verdadeira realidade.", resumiu a deputada estadual eleita no RS. A declaração foi dada em entrevista à Rádio Gaúcha.

Cherini afirmou ainda que pretende conversar com Michele Bolsonaro , presidente do PL Mulher, para entender as declarações da colega de partido.

"Não sabia disso. Até vou me informar, inclusive hoje ( terça-feira ) eu estou indo a Brasília, vou ter uma reunião com a presidente Michele Bolsonaro e vou conversar, vou tentar saber, entender o que acontece sobre isso", afirmou.

O g1 entrou em contato com a assesoria do PL do RS e em Brasília e também procurou a assessoria da deputada Eduarda Campopiano, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem. O espaço segue aberto, e o texto será atualizado caso o partido ou a parlamentar se pronunciem.

Eduarda Campopiano (PL) ganhou projeção política com posições conservadoras e críticas ao feminismo e foi eleita deputada estadual por São Paulo com a maior votação do estado , 1.956.238 votos.

A parlamentar se apresenta como a “maior inimiga das feministas de SP” e ganhou projeção com falas e publicações em redes sociais sobre feminismo , cotas raciais , colonização do Brasil e identidade de gênero , muitas delas em parceria com o deputado federal eleito Lucas Pavanato (PL). Relembre as polêmicas aqui .

Em uma das falas de maior repercussão, Campopiano declarou, em um podcast, que "feminicídio não existe".

"Feminicídio não existe. Feminicídio é uma armadilha semântica. Nenhuma mulher morre por ser mulher", afirmou.

Campopiano também acumula polêmicas por defender a colonização e catequização de povos originários, afirmar que "vestibular não é para ser inclusivo" e por ataques transfóbicos à deputada federal Érika Hilton , a quem chama de "homem biológico".

articles.title: Assalto em Macapá: suspeito é preso ao retornar para o Amapá | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem de 20 anos foi monitorado pela Polícia Civil e localizado no bairro Universidade após o fim da vedação eleitoral. Crime ocorreu no início do ano
articles.summary: Assalto em Macapá: investigado de 20 anos foi monitorado pela Polícia Civil e preso no bairro Universidade após o fim da vedação eleitoral.
articles.body:
Um suspeito de 20 anos investigado por participar de um assalto a mão armada em um comércio no bairro do Trem, na região central de Macapá , foi preso na manhã desta quarta-feira (7), no bairro Universidade, na Zona Sul da capital. O suspeito estava foragido fora do estado e acabou localizado assim que retornou à capital, logo após o fim do período de vedação eleitoral.

O crime aconteceu no início do ano na Avenida Leopoldo Machado. Câmeras de segurança registraram a ação em que quatro suspeitos armados invadiram o estabelecimento, renderam as pessoas no local e levaram o dinheiro do caixa e os pertences dos clientes (veja o vídeo acima) .

Segundo as investigações da Delegacia Especializada em Crimes Contra o Patrimônio (DECCP), um dos assaltantes foi preso em flagrante no dia do crime.

A partir da análise das imagens de segurança, a equipe conseguiu identificar os outros envolvidos e solicitou a prisão preventiva de todos.

“Dois deles fugiram para fora do estado e o outro para uma comunidade do interior. Identificamos o momento em que este indivíduo viria para Macapá na última semana e passamos a monitorá-lo, sendo possível prendê-lo hoje”, explicou o delegado Bruno Braz.

Outro suspeito de integrar o grupo, que também havia fugido do território amapaense, acabou localizado e preso no Estado do Paraná.

Todos os envolvidos foram denunciados pelo Ministério Público do Amapá (MP-AP) e já respondem ao processo como réus na Justiça.

O suspeito preso nesta quarta-feira passará por audiência de custódia e será encaminhado ao Instituto de Administração Penitenciária do Amapá (Iapen), onde permanecerá à disposição do Poder Judiciário.

Suspeito que saiu do estado após assalto a comércio é preso ao retornar a Macapá. — Foto: Polícia Civil/Divulgação

articles.title: Após 70 anos fechado, Cine Rosário será reaberto no Edifício Martinelli, no Centro de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Com investimento de R$ 25 milhões do Grupo Tokyo, o cinema terá projeção em película 35 mm e digital. A programação terá clássicos, filmes em película, debates e sessões especiais, além de peças de teatro e outras apresentações.
articles.summary: Com investimento de R$ 25 milhões do Grupo Tokyo, o cinema terá projeção em película 35 mm e digital. A programação terá clássicos, filmes em película, debates e sessões especiais, além de peças de teatro e outras apresentações.
articles.body:
Imagem do projeto conceitual do Cine Rosário. — Foto: Divulgação/Grupo Tokyo

Depois de 70 anos fechado, o Cine Rosário vai voltar a funcionar no Edifício Martinelli, o primeiro arranha-céu de São Paulo. Inaugurado em 1929, o cinema era considerado um dos mais luxuosos da cidade e fez parte da geração de salas que ajudou a formar a Cinelândia paulistana. As atividades foram encerradas em 1955.

O Grupo Tokyo, responsável pela casa noturna de mesmo nome no Centro, anunciou um investimento de R$ 25 milhões na revitalização do espaço. A previsão é que o cinema seja reaberto em 2028.

🔎 Em março de 2023, o Grupo Tokyo venceu a licitação do Martinelli. O contrato prevê a concessão de quatro andares no topo do edifício, além da Loja 11, na parte térrea, por um período de 15 anos. Hoje, o terraço recebe festas e eventos de vida noturna e também é aberto para visitas guiadas durante o dia.

O novo Cine Rosário vai ocupar o espaço do cinema original, no térreo e no subsolo do prédio, com entrada pela Avenida São João. A sala tinha capacidade para cerca de mil pessoas, mas terá menos lugares na nova versão para atender às exigências atuais de acessibilidade e segurança.

A ideia é fugir do modelo tradicional dos cinemas comerciais. O Rosário não terá vínculo com redes exibidoras e pretende apostar em uma programação voltada principalmente aos cinéfilos, com clássicos, filmes em película, debates e sessões especiais. O espaço também receberá peças de teatro e outras apresentações.

A programação será definida por uma curadoria própria e deve reunir lançamentos, ciclos temáticos, retrospectivas, encontros com diretores, artistas e outros convidados. A sala terá projetores digitais e também equipamento para filmes em película 35 mm.

Para montar o projeto, a equipe do Grupo Tokyo visitou cinemas em diferentes cidades do mundo. Entre as referências estão o Vidiots, em Los Angeles, o Electric Cinema, em Londres, e o Metrograph, em Nova York. São salas que se tornaram pontos de encontro em suas cidades não só pelos filmes exibidos, mas também pela programação e pela experiência de assistir a uma sessão em película.

"O Brasil é o terceiro país com mais usuários no Letterboxd. Temos uma das maiores comunidades de cinéfilos do mundo, mas ainda são poucos os lugares para ela se encontrar. O Rosário nasce para ser esse ponto de encontro, com boa programação, atividades e a experiência de ver um filme em película, numa sala com história", diz Fábio Floriano, CEO e sócio-fundador do Grupo Tokyo.

O espaço passa por estudos de prospecção para identificar o que resta da sala original. Nas primeiras intervenções, a remoção de forros de gesso revelou vestígios de pinturas e elementos decorativos no teto. A extensão da recuperação desses elementos será definida a partir dos estudos técnicos e das diretrizes dos órgãos de patrimônio.

A França convocou o embaixador do Irã nesta quarta-feira (7) por causa do que o porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores francês, Pascal Confavreux, classificou como uma campanha iraniana de desinformação contra o movimento de protestos de estudantes do ensino médio no país.

O diplomata iraniano foi informado sobre o caráter "absolutamente inaceitável" de conteúdos falsos divulgados na internet por contas oficiais do Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Irã, disse Confavreux em um comunicado. Segundo ele, a convocação do embaixador francês em Teerã pelo governo iraniano, na terça-feira (6), não tinha fundamento.

"Essas provocações indignas devem cessar", afirmou.

O Irã convocou na terça-feira o embaixador da França em Teerã por causa dos protestos estudantis em andamento, acusando Paris de "tratamento violento" contra os manifestantes e de cometer violações generalizadas dos direitos humanos, segundo a imprensa estatal iraniana.

articles.standfirst: Animal está sozinho por não ter idade reprodutiva. Centro de Recuperação aos Animais Marinhos orienta que a população mantenha distância e não alimente o visitante.
articles.summary: Animal está sozinho por não ter idade reprodutiva. Centro de Recuperação aos Animais Marinhos orienta que a população mantenha distância e não alimente o visitante
articles.body:
Um elefante-marinho macho e jovem tem sido visto ao longo da faixa de areia na Praia do Cassino , em Rio Grande , no Sul do RS, nos últimos dias.

O animal, que chama a atenção pelo tamanho, foi avistado nas proximidades da antiga passarela de acesso à praia.

Segundo o Centro de Recuperação aos Animais Marinhos (Cram), a aparição não é comum na região. O órgão explica que o elefante-marinho está entrando e saindo da água apenas para descansar . A espécie costuma fazer paradas em praias do litoral durante os deslocamentos e, nestes momentos, precisa de espaço e tranquilidade.

O animal está sozinho porque ainda não tem idade para se reproduzir, período em que os outros indivíduos da espécie estão em fase de reprodução.

A orientação do Cram para quem encontrar o animal ao longo da praia é observar à distância e evitar qualquer tipo de aproximação ou contato. Outra recomendação é não oferecer comida e não tirar fotos com flash.

O órgão reforça que, apesar da aparência calma, o elefante-marinho é um animal silvestre e o descanso faz parte do comportamento natural da espécie.

articles.title: Royal Mail plans to cut 2,500 head office and support function jobs
articles.summary: The postal service firm wants to cut head office and other non-frontline jobs by the end of 2027.
articles.body:
Royal Mail has announced plans to cut 2,500 head office and other supporting roles by the end of 2027 as it battles competition and falling demand for letter deliveries.

The cuts at the postal service will represent about 2% of the 131,000-strong workforce.

However, frontline postal workers - posties and drivers - are not part of the proposed restructuring.

Royal Mail said the workforce reduction, designed to improve efficiency, would be achieved through voluntary redundancies and people choosing to leave the company.

It said the cuts would make it more efficient.

"These proposed changes remove duplication and allow us to invest further in the service we deliver for our customers," said chief executive Alistair Cochrane.

He added that the job cuts "will not be easy, but they are an important part of building a stronger, simpler and future-ready Royal Mail for our customers and colleagues".

Royal Mail said it was in formal consultation with its unions, the Communication Workers Union (CWU) and Unite CMA, over the plans.

The CWU said despite reassurances that there would be no compulsory redundancies, the announcement was "further evidence of a company that is demoralising staff and failing to deliver for customers and the wider community".

"We urge the government to confront the reality of a collapsing Royal Mail and intervene to save this national institution," deputy general secretary Martin Walsh told the BBC.

Unite said Royal Mail, regulator Ofcom, and the government had "failed to address the serious problems facing Royal Mail, especially high competition from gig economy postal services".

The union said the cuts would not improve Royal Mail's quality of service.

Royal Mail has been struggling to meet its delivery targets for first and second class post, and has been fined by the regulator for missing targets in recent years.

Just over 75% of first class letters were delivered on time in the year to the end of March, far off its target of 93%.

Fewer people are sending letters, and the company has repeatedly said that its Universal Service Obligation (USO) – a legal requirement to deliver letters six days a week to every address in the UK – is outdated and needs reform.

Royal Mail, which is a separate from the Post Office, has faced years of criticism from politicians and the public over slow letter deliveries.

In March, postal workers across the UK told the BBC they were being asked to move or hide mail from senior bosses to make it look like delivery targets were being met .

This year, more than 100 MPs have written to regulator Ofcom and the business secretary asking for something to be done about the poor service their constituents say they are receiving.

The firm has said it is investing £500m over the next five years as part of its improvement plan.

Royal Mail is owned by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky's EP Group, after his takeover was approved by shareholders at the end of April last year.

Kretinsky has previously said he will not walk away from the requirement to deliver letters throughout the UK six days a week, as long as he is running the service.

articles.title: Celebrity chef leaves one iconic ingredient out of her cooking and diners can't tell
articles.summary: Maison Ostrow's Paris-born chef creates dairy-free mascarpone, blue cheese and peppercorn sauce alternatives to serve glatt kosher French cuisine.
articles.body: For certain chefs, cooking without butter might sound like culinary sacrilege. But for Olivia Ostrow, it's part of the job. The Paris-born restaurateur and contestant on Food Network's "24 in 24: Last Chef Standing" serves French-Mediterranean cuisine at Maison Ostrow, her kosher restaurant in South Florida, where the meat-based menu means dairy cannot be mixed into dishes. That presents an unusual challenge for a chef working in a cuisine famous for its reliance on butter, cream and cheese. CHEF WHO FLED COMMUNIST COUNTRY OPENS WORLD'S FIRST MICHELIN-STARRED CUBAN RESTAURANT "Can you really make great French food without butter? Yes and no," Ostrow told Fox News Digital. One solution comes from another ingredient long associated with French cooking. "There's a little secret called duck fat," she said. But Ostrow and her culinary team have also developed their own non-dairy versions of ingredients that would otherwise be off-limits. SCIENTISTS MAY HAVE FOUND A WAY TO MAKE SAUSAGE ROLLS AND FLAKY PASTRIES MUCH HEALTHIER "We started making our cheese, and we started our butter," she said. articles.title: ‘Fight won’t be easy’: CJP warns of prolonged agitation ahead of Oct 10 protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organisations on Wednesday called for a united mobilisation against chief election commissioner
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organisations on Wednesday called for a united mobilisation against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar ahead of their October 10 protest, saying the agitation would continue until the electoral system was overhauled.At a joint press conference, the groups sought to put their campaign against the Election Commission (EC) on a broader political footing, backing the opposition INDIA bloc MPs' October 6 protest march and describing the confrontation as one between people defending democracy and the BJP.In July, a CJP-led agitation over the NEET paper leak had forced Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as Union education minister, news agency PTI reported.The group is now seeking to sustain street pressure against Kumar as protests against the EC intensify ahead of October 10.Wednesday's press conference brought together the CJP, All India Students' Association (AISA), All India Students' Federation (AISF) and Students' Federation of India (SFI).The Aam Aadmi Party's student wing, Association of Students for Alternative Politics (ASAP), also participated.CJP co-convener Saurav Das urged people across the country to travel to Delhi and be prepared for a prolonged agitation, PTI reported."This fight is not going to be easy. I appeal to everyone across the country to join us, book train and flight tickets," he said.Das said protesters would not back down even if Kumar resigned, as the electoral system needed cleaning up. He alleged that the BJP's pushback reflected a "lust for eternal power".The demands outlined by Das include Kumar's resignation and initiation of criminal proceedings against him; freezing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls; halting upcoming elections; restoring the January 2025 voters' list and ordering an independent inquiry; and repealing the 2023 law governing appointments to the EC to establish an independent and credible selection process.AISA president Neha Bora said there was no division between the student-led mobilisation and the opposition parties' protests.She said common people, civil society, opposition parties and student organisations stood on one side and the EC and the BJP on the other, PTI reported."There are no divisions. We, the people of India, versus the BJP. If we lead this fight unitedly, we will do it effectively," Bora said.Backing the INDIA bloc MPs who tried to march towards the EC office on Tuesday demanding Kumar's resignation, she said elected representatives had a duty to take to the streets to raise people's issues and defend their rights."That's what the MPs of the INDIA bloc did," she said, adding that the CJP and student organisations of opposition parties would lend strength to the October 10 protest."If ever there was a time to desert the BJP, it is now," Bora said, urging those in the BJP camp to join people seeking to defend democracy and the Constitution.The projection of unity comes days after online sparring between the CJP and sections aligned with the Congress.Das said the participants were united regardless of political affiliations and ideologies in a larger fight to change a "broken system", PTI reported.Asked whether the organisers would obtain permission for the protest, Das said they had submitted a formal intimation at the Parliament Street police station on Wednesday and provided undertakings."Please don't use the word permission. Who is Delhi Police to give us permission?" he said, adding that intimation was sufficient."We will cooperate with Delhi Police and we hope Delhi Police will cooperate with us," he added.SFI's Adarsh Shaji accused Kumar of undermining Indian democracy, describing the confrontation as a fight between "democracy and autocracy".(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Man admits sexually assaulting woman drugged by husband without her knowledge
articles.summary: The husband is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in Greater Manchester.
articles.body:
A man has pleaded guilty to sexually assaulting a woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband without her knowledge for more than 20 years.

The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester.

Sean Peers, 38, was due to stand trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court earlier but admitted one count of assault by penetration on 15 September 2024.

The husband, who has already pleaded guilty to 60 offences against his wife, also admitted a fresh charge of rape and one of sexual assault. Both offences happened last summer.

One of the men accused of joining in the abuse, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee in Scotland, has already pleaded guilty to various offences.

There are a further 11 men due to stand trial who have denied abusing the same woman between 2018 to November 2025.

Peers, from Stockport, was granted conditional bail until sentence, which will take place at the conclusion of the trial involving the other men.

The husband, who is no longer part of the trial as a defendant, will also be sentenced at the conclusion of the case and has been remanded in custody.

A jury was sworn in early in September but the case has faced a series of delays for legal and practical reasons.

On Tuesday the nine women and three men of the jury, plus two female reserve jurors, were told that the husband had provided a witness statement detailing "what it is he says happened" after his guilty pleas.

Judge Maurice Greene said: "That statement is a long statement and that has been disclosed to all defence counsel and it contains a lot of detail."

The judge said the statement contained "lots of pages and lots of documents" and that lawyers in the case were "going through it carefully", which was ongoing work.

The jury were asked to return on Monday 19 October when the prosecution case against the remaining 11 defendants has been scheduled to open.

articles.title: Operation Firewall-2026: ‘Joshita from Mumbai’, ‘Anvi from Delhi’ and the Pakistani spy trap
articles.summary: AMARAVATI: What began as a probe into suspected links between individuals in India and Pakistani intelligence operatives has opened up an alleged
articles.body: AMARAVATI: What began as a probe into suspected links between individuals in India and Pakistani intelligence operatives has opened up an alleged espionage network spanning multiple states, with naval personnel allegedly targeted through fake identities, honeytrap attempts, monetary inducements and digital tools ranging from Indian SIM cards to WhatsApp activation OTPs.Under “Operation Firewall-2026”, the Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence Cell coordinated with police forces across 10 states and Union Territories while probing the alleged network. Of the 18 suspects identified in the case, 13 are naval personnel, police said.At the centre of the investigation are two women PIO identities — “Joshita Pall”, who purportedly presented herself as a ship-building company employee in Mumbai, and “Anvi Mehta”, who allegedly posed as a psychologist based in Delhi.As per news agency PTI, the alleged operation, according to police material, followed a pattern: establish contact through fake social-media profiles, build familiarity and trust, move the conversation to WhatsApp, and then seek sensitive information through messages, voice calls, video calls, honeytrap attempts and monetary inducements.But the network went beyond the identities used to approach naval personnel.Investigators also uncovered an alleged support system involving Indian mobile numbers, SIM cards obtained under Indian names, WhatsApp activation OTPs and cryptocurrency-linked payments.Here is how the alleged spy trap worked:‘Joshita’ from MumbaiTwo alleged female Pakistan Intelligence Operative (PIO) identities emerged in the investigation — “Joshita Pall” and “Anvi Mehta.”According to police, “Joshita Pall” allegedly established initial contact through Facebook and subsequently moved the conversation to WhatsApp.“She purported to be an employee of a ship-building company in Mumbai and sought information about the movement and number of ships and submarines, photographs, and photographs and details of their commanding officers,” said the press release.Monetary inducements were allegedly offered in exchange for such information.‘Anvi’ from DelhiThe second identity, “Anvi Mehta,” allegedly passed herself off as a psychologist based in Delhi.She allegedly attempted to honeytrap naval personnel through voice and video calls, sought photographs of naval ships and sensitive establishments, and attempted to induce personnel to display restricted or sensitive areas during video conversations, said the press release.These identities and the associated communications form part of the alleged modus operandi described in the investigation material.The alleged approach began with social-media contact.Further information shared by a government source to PTI indicated an alleged method involving false social-media identities, honeytrap attempts, monetary inducements, misuse of Indian mobile numbers, WhatsApp activation OTPs and payments facilitated through cryptocurrency channels and intermediaries.Further, persons identified as “female PIOs” allegedly approached defence personnel through fake profiles on Facebook and Instagram.“After establishing familiarity and trust, they shifted communication to Whatsapp and engaged the targets through messages, voice calls and video calls. The alleged approach involved false professional identities, misleading promises, sexually explicit content and monetary inducements intended to draw personnel into sharing sensitive defence information,” the release added.What they wantedThe alleged targets were sought for information going well beyond routine details.The information sought reportedly included the movement and number of naval ships and submarines, photographs and videos of naval assets and sensitive establishments, including photographs and details of commanding officers, police said.Police probe also unearthed attempts to persuade personnel to show sensitive areas of naval establishments, ships and submarines during video calls.Visakhapatnam, which hosts the Eastern Naval Command (ENC), Naval Dockyard, Hindustan Shipyard Ltd (HSL) and Visakhapatnam Port, figures prominently in the case because of the strategic naval and defence establishments located there.The OTP linkThe alleged network also relied on an unusual digital support mechanism — Indian mobile numbers and WhatsApp activation OTPs.Indian mobile numbers and WhatsApp OTPs were allegedly used to facilitate the network and the probe identified a support network involving SIM cards obtained in the country under Indian names and the sharing of mobile-number OTPs with PIOs.“Indian personnel were allegedly offered monetary incentives through cryptocurrency or other intermediaries to share OTPs required to activate whatsapp accounts. Such OTPs were reportedly used to activate whatsapp accounts in Pakistan,” said the press release.These accounts were then allegedly utilised to contact further targets, attempt honey-trapping and collect sensitive defence information.The alleged sharing of activation OTPs is therefore being examined as a means of facilitating the wider espionage network.The money trailThe investigation also identified an alleged financial arrangement in which funds originating from Pakistan were routed through cryptocurrency channels and traders or other intermediaries to persons drawn into the network.The operational diagram accompanying the case material illustrates a suspected flow of funds from PIOs through cryptocurrency deposits and transfers, followed by transactions through intermediaries to compromised persons, said the press release.How the trap workedAccording to the police material, the alleged method depended first on creating familiarity and trust.The fake identities allegedly approached defence personnel through social media, shifted conversations to WhatsApp and then engaged targets through messages, voice calls and video calls.The alleged approach involved false professional identities, misleading promises, sexually explicit content and monetary inducements.In the case of “Anvi Mehta”, police alleged that the identity was used in attempts to honeytrap naval personnel and persuade them to share photographs of naval ships and sensitive establishments or display restricted areas during video conversations.“Joshita Pall”, meanwhile, allegedly sought information about the movement and number of ships and submarines, photographs, and photographs and details of their commanding officers.18 suspects, 13 of them naval personnelOf the total 18 suspects in the espionage conspiracy, 13 are naval personnel who were allegedly indulging in spying prejudicial to national security, police said.The Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence Cell said it acted on credible information that certain individuals were in touch with Pakistani operatives.“The Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence Cell received credible information regarding certain persons in India allegedly maintaining direct contact with Pakistan Intelligence Operatives (PIOs) and their suspected involvement in an espionage conspiracy prejudicial to the national security of India,” it said.“Two suspects were arrested after a prima facie role was established in this case and further investigation is going on for the remaining suspects,” it said.Police arrested Pradeep Mukharjee, a navy employee from the Visakhapatnam naval base, and Annam Sai Varaprasad, a civilian contract driver engaged for naval officers in that city.Mukharjee was arrested recently from Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu. He was produced before a court in Vijayawada and sent to judicial custody till October 14. He is currently lodged in the district jail, Vijayawada.Varaprasad was sent to judicial remand till October 14 and he is also lodged in the same jail.According to police, Varaprasad allegedly shared sensitive and classified information relating to naval and defence establishments with PIOs in return for monetary benefits.Mukharjee was allegedly involved in sharing an OTP for activating a Whatsapp account by a PIO, communicating with the Pakistani operatives, and sharing sensitive information relating to naval and defence establishments.The Counter Intelligence Cell coordinated with police forces of 10 states to zero in on suspects allegedly maintaining direct contact with PIOs.The CI Cell coordinated with 10 states under “Operation Firewall-2026” to probe the suspects for sharing sensitive and classified information on defence establishments and strategic locations.As many as 12 CI Cell teams were deployed across Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Goa, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh and Bihar and Union Territories.In coordination with the concerned states' ATSs (Anti-Terrorist Squads), naval officials and local police, the CI Cell investigation teams examined the complicity of the 18 suspects.Encrypted communicationsThe suspects shared information on Visakhapatnam and other parts of the country through encrypted communication channels, the release said.The police Counter Intelligence Cell seized electronic gadgets as the probe continues on the remaining suspects.OTP warningPolice warned that any person who knowingly shares WhatsApp OTPs with unknown persons for account activation or knowingly shares sensitive defence-related information with unauthorised persons, including suspected PIOs, may face legal action.“The alleged methods described in this case underline the need for vigilance regarding unknown social-media contacts, false professional identities, requests for defence photographs or videos, demands for activation OTPs and offers of money in exchange for information,” said the press release.A case was registered at the Counter Intelligence Police Station in Vijayawada on September 2.It was registered under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, and Official Secrets Act, 1923.“The alleged conspiracy is being investigated for its implications for India's national security, sovereignty and integrity,” the police press release added.The investigation is sensitive and ongoing, police said. They did not divulge details on the rest of the suspects.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Visakhapatnam | Silver Rate in Visakhapatnam | Bank Holidays in Visakhapatnam | Public Holidays in Visakhapatnam | Petrol Price in Visakhapatnam | Diesel Price in Visakhapatnam | CNG Price in Visakhapatnam | LPG Price in VisakhapatnamStay updated with the latest Visakhapatnam news. articles.title: In the 1980s, British civil engineer Tony Deane began digging beneath his family home; 20 years later, the four-level tunnels had a railway and one-tonne lift and are heading to auction from £300,000
articles.summary: From the outside, it looks like an ordinary bungalow tucked away on the outskirts of Reading.
articles.body: From the outside, it looks like an ordinary bungalow tucked away on the outskirts of Reading. There is a garden, a swimming pool and a workshop, nothing to suggest that beneath the property lies a sprawling subterranean world that took two decades to create. Descending more than 15 metres underground are four levels of hand-dug tunnels, complete with rooms, corridors, a railway, a one-tonne goods lift and secret entrances, adds an online report by AOL.A family project undergroundThe extraordinary project was the work of British civil engineer Tony Deane, who began excavating beneath his family home in the 1980s. What started as a personal building project gradually grew into an underground complex covering more than 1,300 sq ft. His six children eventually joined in, turning what might have been a solitary hobby into a remarkable family undertaking, adds the report.There was no fleet of construction machinery involved. The chalk and earth were removed manually, using little more than buckets and wheelbarrows. As the excavation expanded, Deane devised increasingly ingenious ways to move material through the tunnels. Eventually, he installed a railway running through the underground passages, allowing excavated material to be transported more efficiently, explains the report.Four levels below groundAccording to the AOL report, he also constructed a four-level goods lift capable of carrying up to one tonne, connecting the different sections of the subterranean complex. Much of the tunnel system was carved through chalk, a material naturally capable of supporting itself. Where additional reinforcement was necessary, concrete was cast by hand.The property's underground story actually predates the main excavation. In the 1960s, Deane constructed changing rooms beneath the swimming pool. The entrance was concealed behind a striking 23ft rocket standing beside the pool—a feature that remains on the property and provides access to another hidden room, the report adds.Secret doors and a giant rocketAccording to the same report, other concealed spaces are scattered through the complex. One entrance is hidden behind a 1.5-tonne sliding concrete wall, while another lies inside the giant rocket. For years, much of this elaborate underground construction remained known primarily to the family and was hidden beneath the property's workshop.Now heading to auctionNow, the unusual home and its subterranean secrets are set to find a new owner. The property is being offered through BTG Eddisons Property Auctions with a guide price of between £300,000 and £325,000. Above ground, the estate includes a substantial three-storey workshop measuring around 2,500 sq ft, along with parking, gardens, a swimming pool and existing changing rooms. Planning permission granted by West Berkshire Council in December 2024 also allows for a new 5,000-sq-ft, five-bedroom, two-storey house to be constructed on the site of the swimming pool. The workshop has permission to be converted into a three-bedroom home.A property with another life belowBut it is what lies below that is likely to define the property's appeal. The tunnels could potentially serve as secure storage, a private shelter, specialist data infrastructure or simply an extraordinary personal retreat. After decades hidden beneath an unassuming family property, the underground complex is finally coming into the open. It is scheduled to go under the hammer at BTG Eddisons' live-streamed auction on October 28 and 29, the report also adds.For a buyer, the appeal may be difficult to quantify. This is not simply a house with an unusual basement. It is the physical record of a family project that unfolded underground, one bucket of chalk at a time, until an ordinary Berkshire property acquired an extraordinary second life beneath the ground.Image Courtesy: AOLYou use AI every day. articles.title: Bar named in Cornell rape lawsuit disputes accuser's account, says she was never served alcohol while underage
articles.summary: An Ithaca, New York, bar disputed the Cornell University gang-rape accuser's claim it served her alcohol underage on the night of the alleged Chi Phi assault.
articles.body: A bar named in the lawsuit at the center of the Cornell University sexual assault firestorm is disputing the alleged victim's claim that it served her alcohol while she was underage on the night of the alleged assault — a denial the bar has now also lodged in court. Moonies Bar & Nightclub, a downtown Ithaca, New York, bar popular with Cornell students, told Fox News that underage guests at a private Tri Delta sorority event on Oct. 19, 2024, were marked on their hands, while guests over 21 received wristbands. The bar says its bartenders served alcohol only to guests wearing wristbands. The complaint and Moonies' account both say Doe was marked as underage. They differ over whether she was then served alcohol. Doe's lawsuit alleges a Moonies bouncer placed an "X" on each of the then-20-year-old's hands to signify she was under 21, but that she was nevertheless served and consumed at least one alcoholic beverage inside the bar. INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM "No alcohol was served to anyone who had mark on their hands," Moonies said in a statement to Fox News Tuesday, disputing the allegations. CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS Moonies also told Fox News that Doe later worked for the company from February to March 2025 and discussed the October 2024 incident during that period. According to the bar, Doe never said during those conversations that she had been intoxicated at Moonies or served alcohol by one of its bartenders. Fox News Digital contacted Doe's attorney for a response to both of Moonies' assertions. In a formal answer filed Sunday in New York Supreme Court, Zareen Enterprises LLC, which does business as Moonies Bar & Nightclub, denied unlawfully selling or furnishing alcohol to anyone under the legal drinking age and denied selling or furnishing alcohol to any visibly intoxicated person. The filing specifically denies the paragraph of Doe's complaint alleging she was served alcohol at Moonies despite having been marked as underage. Moonies also denied that any act or omission on its part caused Doe's alleged injuries. The bar asked the court to dismiss the complaint against it in its entirety. The dispute comes as the case has roiled Cornell and drawn national attention, with thousands rallying on campus Monday and faculty senators now pushing a no-confidence resolution against the university's central administration over its handling of sexual assault. Gov. Kathy Hochul has also appointed the New York Attorney General's Office as special prosecutor, with Attorney General Letitia James leading an "active criminal investigation." Moonies said it hosted the private Tri Delta event from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m. that night with about 185 guests, including roughly 150 who were over 21 and 35 who were underage. The bar said it had a contract with the sorority and marked underage guests' hands while providing wristbands to those over 21. In the statement, Moonies called Doe's allegation that she was served alcohol "completely inaccurate," saying its employees "strictly followed the rules and did not serve alcohol to any underaged guests." WATCH: CORNELL STUDENTS PROTEST SCHOOL'S HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT INVESTIGATION: CORNELL PICKS FORMER DEPUTY US ATTORNEY GENERAL TO REVIEW SEX ASSAULT RESPONSE In its court filing, Moonies also asserted as affirmative defenses that Doe cannot establish that it unlawfully sold alcohol to an underage or visibly intoxicated person, or that any alleged unlawful sale caused her injuries. The bar maintained that it complied with all applicable laws and regulations governing alcohol sales. The dispute concerns one part of Doe's account of the hours preceding the alleged assault and what happened at Moonies before she arrived at Chi Phi. According to her lawsuit, Doe began the evening drinking vodka at her Tri Delta sorority house before a sorority housemother accompanied her to Moonies. She later went to another Ithaca bar before leaving alone around 11 p.m. and walking to the Chi Phi fraternity house to meet a friend who was a member. By the time she arrived at Chi Phi, Doe was visibly intoxicated and had consumed roughly 10 standard drinks over three hours, according to her complaint. Once inside, Doe alleges she was given another beer before going upstairs, where two fraternity members pressured her into snorting what they said was ketamine, a drug she says she had never previously taken. She alleges they also gave her marijuana and high-proof liquor before sexual activity began. Doe alleges other fraternity members became involved as the night progressed and that she eventually became "completely incapacitated." Seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers are accused in her lawsuit of sexual assault and rape. The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining that sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men. The case burst into public view when Doe filed the 101-page lawsuit Sept. 16, nearly two years after the alleged encounter. In addition to the seven former fraternity members, Doe sued Cornell University, Chi Phi and affiliated entities, her own Tri Delta sorority and Moonies, among others, alleging that institutions around her failed to protect her before, during and after the events of that night. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The lawsuit's allegations prompted renewed scrutiny of the original criminal investigation. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who initially declined to pursue charges, has said the six-page sworn statement his office received from Cornell University Police in 2024 did not allege that Doe was drugged against her will or gang-raped and instead described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual." A fuller transcript of Doe's November 2024 police interviews later obtained by CBS New York included statements in which she distinguished the initial sexual encounter from later activity and explicitly told investigators she had been raped. Van Houten said his office had never received that transcript. Fox News' Michelle Langer contributed to this report.

articles.title: Ex-bankers jailed for rigging rates have convictions quashed
articles.summary: Jay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon, Colin Bermingham had their convictions overturned by the Court of Appeal.
articles.body:
Five former Barclays traders sentenced in one of the biggest scandals of the financial crisis have had their convictions overturned following a long-running legal battle.

Jay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon, Colin Bermingham were convicted following trials for manipulating the interest rates used for loans between banks.

But their convictions were quashed on Wednesday by the Court of Appeal. The ruling came after two other former City traders had their convictions overturned last year, which paved the way for others to appeal.

The traders were cast by prosecutors as a symbol of banker greed amid public backlash and anger during the 2008 financial crisis.

Merchant, Mathew, Pabon and Bermingham have all served various jail terms. Moryoussef was sentenced in his absence in 2018, never returned to the UK to serve time after France refused to extradite him.

The prosecutions were over the manipulation of two key interest rate mechanisms: Libor and Euribor, which at the time were used to set borrowing costs on a range of loans such as mortgages and car finance deals.

Mathew said the "strain" of what he had gone through had been a burden on him for the last 10 years.

"Having this conviction quashed is not simply about correcting the record, it's about finally having validation that this is an injustice that never should have happened," the 45-year-old said.

"I now have two children and this means a great deal to have the record corrected for their sake as well."

Merchant, 55, added that he looked forward to moving on with his life, but said part of that would be "ensuring that those responsible for what happened are held fully accountable".

Lord Justice Edis said full reasons behind the overturned convictions would be given later on Wednesday.

City traders have rate-rigging convictions quashed

Rate 'rigging' traders say they were scapegoated - now the Supreme Court will decide

The financial crisis began in 2008, sending huge economic shockwaves across the world and triggering recessions in many countries.

There was a public backlash against bankers, held by many to be responsible for the crisis, while the financial sector was protected by taxpayer-funded bailouts.

The Libor scandal erupted in 2012, when it was discovered that at the outbreak of the financial crisis, banks had been misrepresenting their positions during the process of setting the lending rate, helping to boost profits and mask difficulties.

Some 19 City traders were convicted in the US and UK between 2015 and 2019 across nine criminal trials held in London and New York.

Each of the former Barclays traders in Wednesday's successful appeal had originally been convicted of a single count of conspiracy to defraud as result of alleged attempts to influence financial benchmark rates.

Two other bankers have already had their names cleared.

Tom Hayes, a former trader at Swiss bank UBS, was the first banker jailed. He won a 10-year legal battle last year to have his conviction overturned at the Supreme Court in July 2025.

His victory alongside that of fellow trader Carlo Palombo, who was jailed in 2019, paved the way for others to challenge their convictions.

Hayes and Palombo argued they were wrongly prosecuted for what were normal commercial practices in order to appease public anger towards the banks over the financial crisis.

Pabon, 48, who had his name cleared on Wednesday, hailed Hayes for his refusal to "let it go". He had "pushed this through" for the rest of them, he said.

The Serious Fraud Office (SFO), which brought the original case against the traders, has not opposed the appeals.

Barclays bank has been contacted for comment.

The latest ruling means just two traders still have convictions over interest rate rigging - former Deutsche Bank trader Christian Bittar and former Barclays trader Peter Johnson.

Bittar was jailed in 2018 after pleading guilty and served two years in prison. He will challenge his conviction on 9 October.

Johnson was the original whistleblower calling attention to the Libor scandal but pleaded guilty on advice that he had little chance of winning at trial. He also hopes to appeal.

articles.body: A 45-year-old GP who was reportedly part of a pool of doctors treating members of the British royal family -- Queen Camilla -- was found dead at her home near the Sandringham Estate in Norfolk, with her husband later charged with her murder. Dr Hannah Cain, who was known professionally as Dr Hannah Terry, was found at the couple’s home in Fern Hill, Dersingham, in the early hours of October 4. Her husband, Mark Cain, 45, was arrested and charged with murder.Cain appeared before Norwich Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday. He was not asked to enter a plea and spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address. He was remanded in custody and is due to appear at King’s Lynn Crown Court.The court heard that ambulance services contacted police at around 2.25am after Dr Cain was found unconscious and not breathing in an upstairs bedroom. She was reportedly among a group of GPs regularly available to members of the royal family when they were staying at nearby Sandringham and was believed to have treated senior royals, including Queen Camilla. The medical centre was temporarily closed following her death, citing "extremely difficult circumstances affecting our practice team". The Sun reported, citing sources, that King Charles and Queen Camilla had been informd about the murder. Dr Cain's friend said she seemed worried which was out of character.Cain had previously worked at Heacham GP Surgery for nine years before moving to Grimston Medical Centre.
